image_description: A close-up, low-angle shot of a hammerhead shark swimming in dark blue water. The shark is viewed from below and the side, highlighting its white ventral surface and the underside of its distinctive cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head). The eye is visible at the tip of the hammer. Other sharks are visible in the blurred background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic T-shaped head structure characteristic of hammerhead sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is distinctly located at the very end of the lateral extension of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostrils are located on the anterior/ventral side of the cephalofoil and are not visible from this specific viewing angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior edge is facing away from the camera or obscured by the angle; only the ventral and posterior aspects are clearly visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the torso shows a smooth, tapered shape consistent with a streamlined aquatic body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral side is bright white. While the dorsal side is mostly out of frame, the visible transition at the flank suggests standard countershading.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image resolution and lighting smooth out the skin texture; individual dermal denticles are not resolvable.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is on the top of the shark and is completely occluded by the body in this ventral-side view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One pectoral fin is clearly visible in the lower right, appearing broad and triangular as expected.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the frame or heavily blurred in the background.

artifact_observations.location: Ventral surface of the main shark's body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The white underbelly appears excessively smooth and plastic-like, lacking the subtle micro-texture or pore details expected in a high-fidelity macro shot of shark skin, though this may be due to lighting/specular highlights.

The background sharks appear somewhat 'melted' or indistinct. The separation between the dorsal fin and the body of the background shark is blurry and lacks clear structural definition, typical of AI depth-of-field artifacts.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and rule out generic shark misclassifications.
To verify the continuity of the cephalofoil and ensure no floating artifacts or boundary bleeding with the water.
To assess the realism of the skin texture and lighting, specifically checking for the 'plastic' look noted in artifacts.

focus_areas: Cephalofoil structural integrity and eye placement
Skin texture realism (dermal denticles vs. smooth plastic)
Boundary sharpness between shark and water
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the texture of the white underbelly. Real shark skin has a specific grain even when wet and lit. If it looks like smooth porcelain or plastic, flag it as a texture anomaly. Also, verify that the eye at the tip of the hammer connects logically to the head structure without any 'melting' or weird blending.
